title: Module 3 - Model Evaluation and Explainability Test

questions.question: Which metric measures the proportion of all predictions that were correct?
A medical test identifies 90 sick patients correctly but also marks 30 healthy people as sick. Which metric is directly affected by these false positives?
Recall answers the question:
options: Of all predicted positives, how many were correct?
How many total predictions were correct?
Of all actual positives, how many did the model find?
How close are predicted values to actual values?

questions.question: Which metric provides a balance between precision and recall?
A spam detector catches every spam email but also marks many genuine emails as spam. The model most likely has:
In a highly imbalanced dataset, accuracy can be misleading because:
options: A model can achieve high accuracy by predicting only the majority class

questions.question: Which metric is commonly used for regression problems?
What does Mean Absolute Error (MAE) measure?
options: The average absolute difference between predictions and actual values

questions.question: Compared to MAE, Mean Squared Error (MSE) penalizes:
A model predicts house prices. One prediction is off by ₹50,000 while another is off by ₹5,000. Which metric will punish the ₹50,000 error disproportionately more?
The R² (coefficient of determination) score measures:
options: The proportion of variance explained by the model

questions.question: An R² score of 1 indicates:
options: The model performs worse than random guessing
The model explains none of the variance
A perfect fit to the data

questions.question: Error analysis is primarily performed to:
options: Understand why the model makes mistakes
Reduce the number of features automatically

questions.question: A classifier consistently mistakes cats for dogs but rarely confuses dogs for birds. This observation is an example of:
Which tool is especially useful for analyzing classification errors across classes?
A model predicts every patient as healthy in a disease dataset where only 2% are sick. The model achieves 98% accuracy. What is the biggest issue?
options: Accuracy is misleading because recall for sick patients is very poor.
The model has perfect F1 score.

questions.question: Which metric would be most important for a cancer detection system where missing a positive case is extremely dangerous?
Which metric would be most important for an email spam filter where incorrectly marking genuine emails as spam should be minimized?
After performing error analysis, a data scientist discovers that most mistakes occur in low-light images. What is the MOST reasonable next step?
options: Collect more low-light training data or improve preprocessing

questions.question: Which sequence best represents a mature machine learning evaluation workflow?
options: Train → Compute metrics → Analyze errors → Improve the model

questions.question: A weather model predicts a 70% chance of rain on 100 different days. If the model is perfectly calibrated, approximately how many of those days should actually experience rain?
Probability calibration primarily measures whether:
A classifier predicts 99% confidence for almost every prediction but is correct only 80% of the time. This model is:
Which statement best describes an underconfident model?
options: It gives probabilities that are too high.
It gives probabilities lower than the actual correctness frequency.

questions.question: Why is probability calibration important in medical diagnosis systems?
options: Doctors need reliable confidence estimates to make decisions.

questions.question: What is uncertainty in machine learning?
options: The inability to train a model
The possibility that a prediction may be wrong
The number of features in a dataset

questions.question: Which situation demonstrates high uncertainty?
options: The model always predicts the same label.

questions.question: An autonomous vehicle detects an object and assigns only 52% confidence to its prediction. The safest action is likely to:
options: Treat the prediction cautiously and slow down
Assume the object does not exist

questions.question: Why do AI systems need to estimate uncertainty?
options: To know when predictions may be unreliable

questions.question: A facial recognition system predicts an identity with only 35% confidence. A well-designed system should:
Confidence in machine learning predictions generally refers to:
options: How certain the model is about its prediction

questions.question: A bank's fraud detection model assigns 98% confidence that a transaction is fraudulent. What is the most reasonable action?
options: Investigate or temporarily block the transaction

questions.question: Decision-making systems often use confidence thresholds because:
options: Low-confidence predictions may require human review.

questions.question: A model is perfectly calibrated. Out of all predictions made with 80% confidence, approximately what percentage should be correct?
Which application requires both accurate predictions and reliable confidence estimates the MOST?
A model predicts with high confidence but is frequently wrong. This indicates:
Which statement best describes the relationship between confidence and decision making?
options: Higher confidence often leads to stronger automated decisions.

questions.question: A medical AI only gives automatic diagnoses when confidence exceeds 95%. Predictions below this threshold are sent to doctors. This is an example of:
Which statement about uncertainty is TRUE?
options: A model can never be uncertain.
Uncertainty estimation helps prevent risky decisions.
Uncertainty always means the model is bad.

questions.question: An AI assistant gives two answers: one with 55% confidence and another with 97% confidence. A rational decision system should:
options: Prefer the prediction with higher confidence while considering calibration
Always choose the lower confidence prediction

questions.question: What is the primary goal of Explainable AI (XAI)?
options: To make AI models train faster
To reduce the size of datasets
To help humans understand why AI made a particular decision

questions.question: Why is explainability especially important in medical AI systems?
options: Doctors need to trust and understand the reasoning behind predictions

questions.question: An AI system rejects a loan application but cannot explain why. This situation illustrates the problem of:
Which statement best describes a 'black-box' AI model?
options: A model that uses only numerical data
A model whose internal reasoning is difficult for humans to understand
A model that cannot make predictions

questions.question: Feature importance refers to:
options: The number of features in a dataset
How strongly each feature influences a model's prediction
The order in which features are collected

questions.question: A house-price prediction model considers location more influential than the number of bedrooms. This is an example of:
Why is feature importance useful?
options: It helps explain which inputs contributed most to a prediction

questions.question: An AI predicts that a student will pass an exam mainly because of attendance and previous scores. Attendance and previous scores are:
Which feature would likely have high importance in a model predicting whether it will rain?
What does fairness in AI primarily aim to achieve?
options: Equal and unbiased treatment of individuals or groups

questions.question: An AI hiring system consistently favors one gender despite equal qualifications. This is an example of:
Why can biased training data lead to unfair models?
options: The model learns patterns, including unfair ones, from the data
The model ignores the training data

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a fairness concern?
options: A model takes too long to train
A recommendation system uses too much memory
A credit approval model unfairly rejects applicants from a specific region
A model uses too many features

questions.question: Why is explainability often connected to fairness?
options: Understanding a model's decisions can help identify unfair behavior
Only explainable models can be trained

questions.question: A healthcare model gives different recommendations to identical patients because of their ethnicity. This indicates:
Which statement about feature importance is TRUE?
options: Some features may have little or no effect on predictions.
Feature importance exists only in regression models.

questions.question: An AI model predicts loan defaults. Income has very high importance, while favorite color has almost no importance. This suggests:
options: The model has learned meaningful relationships
The model cannot explain its predictions

questions.question: Which question is MOST related to explainable AI?
options: How many GPUs were used for training?
Why did the model classify this email as spam?

questions.question: A university uses an AI system for admissions. To ensure responsible AI, administrators should be concerned about:
options: Both explainability and fairness of decisions

questions.question: Which sequence best represents responsible AI development?
options: Build model → Analyze feature importance → Check fairness → Deploy
